_comment: Trigger cases test description routing only. Hard negatives are drawn from the three
neighbouring SDD skills, because those are the realistic mis-routes: 'plan the product'
plausibly matches all four. Behavior cases are run in a live session; grade the artifact

trigger.prompt: Draft our durable product vision and North Star statement
Write a PR-FAQ for this product so we can pressure-test the customer benefit
Produce a Lean Canvas covering the problem, segments and unfair advantage
Define the durable product capabilities CAP-* and quality attributes QA-*
Reframe our product strategy: who we serve, the core problem, and what we will never build
A milestone invalidated a core assumption, so revise the product statement
Our vision is a slogan with no teeth — sharpen it so it decides what not to build
Sequence the remaining milestones on Now/Next/Later horizons by risk
Revalidate the roadmap now that the db-schema-migrations milestone shipped
Write the REQ-* requirements baseline with EARS acceptance for the aws-deployment milestone
Produce the Layer 1 detailed planning and ADRs for this milestone
Implement the code-ready engineering tasks for slice 2 and record the closeout
Decompose this milestone into delivery stories for the first vertical slice

behavior.prompt: Read the material under docs/ and draft docs/specs/PRODUCT_STATEMENT.md. Ask clarifying questions first, then validate with a PR-FAQ.
expected_behavior: Asks 3-7 concrete elicitation questions before drafting, or records an explicit Assumptions subsection when told to proceed
Produces all nine required sections in order
Gives every QA-* a response measure, and every CAP-* a why and a measurable success signal
Keeps stack, schema and architecture decisions out of the file
Records one validation lens plus the adversarial critique pass inline
States the handoff to create-product-roadmap and whether the current-state docs were seeded

behavior.prompt: The last milestone showed that our exact-backend scaling assumption was wrong. Update the product statement.
expected_behavior: Treats the statement as durable and changes only what the evidence invalidated
Preserves existing CAP-*/QA-* ids rather than renumbering; marks anything retired as superseded with a reason
Appends a dated Change log entry naming the triggering milestone
Re-states that create-product-roadmap revalidation must follow

behavior.prompt: Review our product statement and tell me what is too vague to guide a roadmap.
expected_behavior: Answers the question instead of rewriting the file
Names specific CAP-* that are outputs rather than outcomes, and QA-* missing a response measure
Flags any architecture or stack detail that belongs in ARCHITECTURE_OVERVIEW.md or TECH_STACK.md
Points at assumptions with no kill criterion
